content: 1. The gastrointestinal (GI) tract anatomy progresses from proximal to distal as follows: duodenum, jejunum, ileum, appendix, colon, sigmoid colon, and rectum. 2. The brachial plexus is organized into roots, trunks, divisions, cords, and branches. 3. The cranial nerves are as follows: I: Olfactory nerve II: Optic nerve III: Oculomotor nerve IV: Trochlear nerve V: Trigeminal nerve VI: Abducens nerve VII: Facial nerve VIII: Acoustic (vestibulocochlear) nerve IX: Glossopharyngeal nerve X: Vagus nerve XI: Accessory nerve XII: Hypoglossal nerve 4. Extraocular muscle innervation: The lateral rectus muscle is innervated by cranial nerve VI (abducens). The superior oblique muscle is innervated by cranial nerve IV (trochlear). All other extraocular muscles are innervated by cranial nerve III (oculomotor). 5. The branches of the facial nerve include the temporal, zygomatic, buccal, mandibular, and cervical branches. 6. The penis is innervated by branches of the pudendal nerve, which originates from spinal cord levels S2-S4. Parasympathetic innervation facilitates erection, while sympathetic innervation facilitates ejaculation. 7. The aortic arch gives rise to the following branches: B: Brachiocephalic trunk C: Left common carotid artery S: Left subclavian artery 8. The femoral triangle contains, in order: nerve, artery, vein, empty space, and lymphatics. The femoral sheath encloses the artery, vein, and lymphatics. 9. The phases of cell division are: Prophase Metaphase Anaphase Telophase 10. The cell cycle stages include: G1 phase: Growth phase 1 S phase: DNA synthesis G2 phase: Growth phase 2 M phase: Mitosis C phase: Cytokinesis 11. The Golgi complex functions to distribute proteins and lipids from the endoplasmic reticulum, add mannose to lysosomal proteins, sulfate sugars and tyrosine, assemble proteoglycans, add O-linked oligosaccharides to serine and threonine, and modify N-linked oligosaccharides on asparagine. 12. Collagen synthesis and function involve: C-terminal propeptide (procollagen) and covalent cross-linking, requiring vitamin C and copper as cofactors. Collagen functions extracellularly and is associated with osteoblasts, connective tissue, and cartilage. Lysyl hydroxylase and lysyl oxidase are enzymes involved in collagen cross-linking. Collagen fibers are long, triple-helical structures formed by hydrogen bonding of alpha chains. Glycine is present in every third position of the collagen sequence. Collagen is glycosylated and assembled in the Golgi apparatus before being secreted. Collagen is a major component of the extracellular matrix and is associated with conditions such as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and osteogenesis imperfecta. 13. Carbon monoxide inhibits cytochrome oxidase in the electron transport chain. 14. A rightward shift in the hemoglobin-oxygen dissociation curve is caused by increased carbon dioxide, acidosis (low pH), increased 2,3-DPG, exercise, and elevated temperature. 15. G-protein receptors are classified as follows: Q: Alpha-1 I: Alpha-2 S: Beta-1 S: Beta-2 Q: M1 I: M2 Q: M3 16. Adrenaline activates beta receptors, leading to an increase in cyclic AMP. 17. Enzymes are classified into six categories: oxidoreductases, transferases, hydrolases, isomerases, ligases, and lyases. 18. The enzymes involved in glycolysis include hexokinase, phosphohexose isomerase, phosphofructokinase-1, aldolase, triose phosphate isomerase, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, phosphoglycerate kinase, phosphoglycerate mutase, enolase, and pyruvate kinase. 19. The steps of glycolysis are: glucose → glucose-6-phosphate → fructose-6-phosphate → fructose-1,6-bisphosphate → dihydroxyacetone phosphate → glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate → 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate → 3-phosphoglycerate → 2-phosphoglycerate → phosphoenolpyruvate → pyruvate. 20. Metabolic processes such as heme synthesis, the urea cycle, and gluconeogenesis occur in both the cytoplasm and mitochondria. 21. Amino acids that form acetyl-CoA or acetoacetyl-CoA include lysine, tryptophan, leucine, and isoleucine. 22. The citric acid cycle involves the following compounds: oxaloacetate, citrate, isocitrate, alpha-ketoglutarate, succinyl-CoA, succinate, fumarate, and malate. 23. The enzymes of the citric acid cycle include citrate synthase, aconitase, isocitrate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, succinyl-CoA synthetase, succinate dehydrogenase, fumarase, and malate dehydrogenase. 24. Essential amino acids include phenylalanine, valine, threonine, tryptophan, isoleucine, methionine, histidine, arginine, leucine, and lysine. Arginine and histidine are semi-essential. 25. Creatine phosphate is synthesized from glycine, arginine, and methionine. 26. The catabolism of branched-chain amino acids involves transamination, oxidative decarboxylation, and dehydrogenation. 27. Skeletal muscle utilizes branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, and valine) during fasting. 28. The urea cycle includes ornithine, carbamoyl phosphate, citrulline, aspartate, argininosuccinate, fumarate, arginine, and urea. 29. Pyrimidine nucleotides include cytosine, uracil, and thymine. 30. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency can lead to hemolytic anemia when exposed to oxidant drugs such as sulfonamides, primaquine, and certain antipyretics. 31. Pompe’s disease is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-1,4-glucosidase deficiency. 32. Galactosemia results from a deficiency in galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase. 33. Fabry’s disease is characterized by foam cells in the kidneys, febrile episodes, alpha-galactosidase A deficiency, angiokeratomas, burning pain in extremities, renal failure, and an X-linked recessive inheritance pattern. 34. Hurler syndrome features include hepatosplenomegaly, coarse facial features, autosomal recessive inheritance, alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency, corneal clouding, developmental delay, and short stature. 35. Acute intermittent porphyria presents with abdominal pain, polyneuropathy, psychological abnormalities, pink urine, and drug-induced exacerbations. 36. Vitamin B deficiencies include: B1 (thiamine): Beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome. B2 (riboflavin): Angular stomatitis and glossitis. B3 (niacin): Pellagra (diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia, and death). 37. Folate deficiency can result from alcoholism, folic acid antagonists, oral contraceptives, low dietary intake, infections, celiac disease, or pregnancy. 38. Fat-soluble vitamins include A, D, E, and K. 39. Hypervitaminosis A can cause headache, hepatomegaly, anorexia, alopecia, bone pain, dry skin, and drowsiness. 40. The APGAR score evaluates newborns based on appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, and respiration, with a maximum score of 10.
